summary: Google publishes no original-MMLU or GSM8K score for Gemma 4 26B A4B; the model card (revision 4d7ae4984b7d) reports MMLU-Pro, MMMLU, GPQA Diamond, AIME 2026, LiveCodeBench v6 and BigBench Extra Hard for the instruction-tuned bf16 model, and labels only the Gemma 3 27B comparison column 'no think'. None of these setups matches this harness (zero-shot, thinking disabled, greedy, ~4-bit weights, answer-prefilled MMLU, 512-token GSM8K cap), so they are context, not a pass/fail threshold; the frameworks are judged against each other on identical items.

results.setup: Google model card (Gemma 3 27B column marked 'no think'; Gemma 4 columns not)

notes: Order-of-magnitude check: the same table puts 26B A4B 22.6 points above E2B on MMLU Pro. This harness measured 57-61% MMLU and 76-78% GSM8K for E2B on the identical subsets (2026-10-02 CPU report), so a healthy 26B A4B configuration should score clearly higher on both.

The 26B A4B chat template closes a non-thinking model turn with an empty thought channel ('<|channel>thought\n<channel|>'); the model card states that all Gemma 4 models except E2B/E4B emit this empty block when thinking is disabled. This suite's prompts include it (workload.chat_template = gemma4-empty-thought).
Published scores use bf16 weights; no source reports accuracy for the QAT Q4_0 GGUF, the LiteRT-LM GPU package, the MLX 4-bit conversion or the BaseRT Q4 bundle themselves.
